bibliographic.title: Does Public Accountability Work?: An Assessment Tool
bibliographic.authors: Bovens, M.A.P.; 't Hart, P.; Schillemans, T.
bibliographic.citation_apa: Bovens, M. A. P., 't Hart, P., & Schillemans, T. (2008). Does public accountability work?: An assessment tool. Public Administration, 86(1), 225-242. https://doi.org/10.1111/j.1467-9299.2008.00716.x

methodology.method_family: multicriteria normative assessment framework with illustrative case application
methodology.study_design: conceptual instrument development demonstrated through analysis of boards of oversight of agencies
methodology.sample_description: illustrative application to boards of oversight of agencies
methodology.technology_context: public accountability arrangements in government and agencies; no AI or LLM technology discussed

eligibility.decision_rationale: The article develops and demonstrates a multicriteria tool for assessing public accountability arrangements in government. It is strongly relevant to accountability, governance, oversight, dialogue, and regulated public-sector contexts, but contains no LLM, generative AI, chatbot, agent, RAG, or conversational-system technology. It should inform conceptual framing rather than serve as central empirical evidence on conversational governance in LLM-based systems.

appraisal.notes: Appraisal based on partial text provided. The study clearly states its objective and methodological approach, but limited excerpts restrict assessment of sampling, data collection detail, limitations discussion, and ethics/reflexivity.

cerqual.explanation: The accountability framework is conceptually coherent and well specified in the available text, but its direct relevance to LLM-based conversational governance is indirect. Adequacy for the review is moderate as foundational context; empirical fit to the review's technology focus is low.

coding.subtheme: Multicriteria normative framework for evaluating accountability arrangements

synthesis.main_claim: Public accountability arrangements can be systematically assessed using a multicriteria tool grounded in democratic, constitutional, and learning perspectives, and the authors demonstrate this tool through analysis of boards of oversight of agencies.
synthesis.contribution: Provides a structured yardstick to evaluate whether accountability arrangements work, moving debate beyond impressionistic claims of accountability deficits or overloads.
synthesis.limitations: Provided text does not fully expose study limitations, empirical breadth, or validation beyond the illustrative case of oversight boards.
synthesis.use_in_review: Use as foundational contextual evidence for accountability, forum-actor relations, questioning, judgment, consequences, stakeholder dialogue, and oversight in regulated public administration. Do not use as central evidence on conversational governance or LLM systems.

evidence.claim: Article develops a systematic assessment instrument for public accountability arrangements
evidence.excerpt: In this article we develop an instrument for systematically assessing public accountability arrangements, drawing on three different normative perspectives.

evidence.claim: Research type is methodological instrument development with illustrative application
evidence.excerpt: We demonstrate the use of our multicriteria assessment tool in an analysis of a new accountability arrangement: the boards of oversight of agencies.

evidence.claim: Accountability is defined as a forum-actor relationship involving explanation, questioning, judgment, and consequences
evidence.excerpt: Accountability, defined here as ' the relationship between an actor and a forum, in which the actor has an obligation to explain and justify his or her conduct, the forum can pose questions and pass judgment, and the actor may face consequences '

evidence.claim: Three normative perspectives structure the assessment tool
evidence.excerpt: In the democratic perspective, accountability arrangements should effectively link government actions to the ' democratic chain of delegation ' . In the constitutional perspective, it is essential that accountability arrangements prevent or uncover abuses of public authority. In the learning perspective, accountability is a tool to make governments effective in delivering on their promises.

evidence.claim: Assessment criteria include interaction and dialogue between forums and executive actors
evidence.excerpt: Does the accountability forum have incentives to engage executive actors in relevant questioning and debate and is their interaction focused on conformity of actions with laws and norms?

evidence.claim: Learning perspective emphasizes ongoing consequential dialogue with stakeholders
evidence.excerpt: Does the accountability arrangement provide a setting and a set of interaction routines which induces ongoing, consequential dialogue among executive actors and key stakeholders about performance feedback?

evidence.claim: Illustrative case concerns oversight boards in public administration
evidence.excerpt: We demonstrate the use of our multicriteria assessment tool in an analysis of a new accountability arrangement: the boards of oversight of agencies.

evidence.claim: No LLM, generative AI, or conversational-system technology is present in the provided text
evidence.excerpt: In recent years, there has been a drive to strengthen existing public accountability arrangements and to design new ones.

evidence.claim: Published in peer-reviewed journal Public Administration
